Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The home page is easy to read on a phone, but the room details are halfway down a long announcement, and several members have asked whether the club still meets in the upstairs gallery. Our coordinator, Maya Chen, said, “The gallery is open, but the building entrance changes after six.” I am forwarding the revised room schedule to the web volunteer so the page can show the entrance note beside the meeting time rather than at the bottom.

The schedule covers the next six weeks and lists three kinds of gatherings. The Thursday novel discussion meets at 6:30 in the upstairs gallery. The Saturday family reading hour starts at 10 in the courtyard room, and the monthly quiet reading session takes place on the first Monday at 5:45 in the small studio. The website currently gives the Thursday time but calls every other event a special session. Visitors have mistaken that phrase for a cancellation. The new schedule names each event and gives the room as well as the start time. The branch phone number remains unchanged and belongs in the contact box.

The web volunteer asked me to send the details in one message instead of forwarding three separate calendar notices. I checked the dates against the printed board beside the front desk and against the library's shared calendar. The first Thursday is April 11, and the last listed gathering is May 20. The courtyard room has a different entrance from the main library door, and the gallery entrance is reached from the east stairwell. People who use the ramp should go through the side door and ask the desk attendant to unlock the lift. These directions are already on the building page, but the room schedule needs a short link to that page.

The monthly quiet reading session has a condition that matters for the later meetings. If the studio is booked for a children's workshop, the club will meet in the gallery instead, and the website should say that a room change will be posted by noon on the day of the session. The booking calendar currently shows the studio as available for May 6, but the library manager has not confirmed that date. The first Monday in April is April 1, and the first Monday in May is May 6. The note should apply to May 6 only unless the manager reports another conflict, and nobody should present the room change as confirmed.

The update also needs the practical details members use when they arrive:
1. Put the meeting date and start time in the first line of each event listing.
2. Include the room name and the correct entrance note for that room.
3. Link the accessibility directions instead of copying the full directions into every listing.
4. Keep the general contact number in the contact box, and do not replace it with a volunteer's personal number.
5. Add the noon update note to the May 6 quiet reading session only.
The volunteer can adjust line breaks after the information is in place, but the words for the room condition need to remain visible on a phone.

At last week's discussion, two visitors arrived at the main door just before seven and found a paper notice pointing them around the side of the building. One member suggested adding a photograph of each entrance to the website, but the club does not have recent pictures of the east stairwell or the courtyard entrance. The building page already has a simple map with both doors marked, and the desk attendant confirmed that the map is current. Maya said, “A map is better than an old photograph if the signs move again.” The schedule can link to the map without adding a new image.

The volunteer also wants to know whether the event titles can be shortened for the calendar display. The title “family reading hour” should stay as written because parents search for those words, and the quiet reading session is distinct from the silent study hours offered by the library. The Thursday novel discussion can appear as “novel discussion” on the calendar tile, but the full event title should remain on the event page. The schedule does not need book titles because the group chooses each novel during the prior meeting. If a title is selected before the page is updated, it can be added later by the coordinator.

I compared the revised schedule with the paper copy and found that the paper copy gives the Saturday event as beginning at 10:15. The calendar says 10, and the room reservation begins at 9:45. Maya checked with the family reading host and confirmed that 10 is the public start time. The earlier reservation is for setting out chairs and picture books. This distinction should not be added to the public listing because visitors only need the time they are welcome to arrive. The paper copy can be corrected at the next print run, but the website update should use the confirmed calendar time.

Before forwarding the schedule, I read the contact details aloud and checked the spelling of Riverside branch and Maya Chen. The phone number is 555 0148, and the volunteer address is readingweb at riverlibrary dot org. The address belongs to the shared volunteer account and not to Maya personally. I am forwarding the revised schedule with the map link and the note about the May 6 room still awaiting confirmation. After the volunteer places it on the site, I will compare the page with the printed schedule at the front desk. The next club meeting is Thursday, April 11, and the gallery entrance note should be visible before members leave the home page."}]
